---
title: "Model"
---

## Overview

SpaxNMF represents an IFU cube as a matrix \(X \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}^{n \times p}\),
with one row per spaxel and one column per wavelength channel. The model seeks
a low-rank non-negative factorization

$$
X \approx AS
$$

where:

- \(A \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}^{n \times k}\) contains component weights for each spaxel
- \(S \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}^{k \times p}\) contains the component spectra
- \(k\) is the chosen factorization rank

`A` should be interpreted simply as a set of component-weight maps over the
field.

## Objective Function

The current implementation minimizes

$$
\mathcal{L}(A,S)=
\|X-AS\|_F^2
+\lambda_S \|DS\|_F^2
+\sum_c \lambda_{A,c}\sum_{i,j} w_{ij}(A_{ic}-A_{jc})^2
+\sum_c \lambda_{C,c}\|A_{:,c}\|_1
$$

with Gaussian spatial couplings

$$
w_{ij} = \exp\left(-\frac{d_{ij}^2}{2\sigma^2}\right).
$$

<div class="feature-grid">
<div class="feature-card">
<h3>Reconstruction term</h3>
<p>
\(\|X-AS\|_F^2\) matches the model to the observed spectra.
</p>
</div>
<div class="feature-card">
<h3>Spectral smoothness</h3>
<p>
\(\lambda_S \|DS\|_F^2\) penalizes channel-to-channel roughness in the recovered
component spectra.
</p>
</div>
<div class="feature-card">
<h3>Spatial coherence</h3>
<p>
\(\lambda_{A,c}\) controls how strongly nearby spaxels are encouraged to carry
similar weights for component \(c\).
</p>
</div>
</div>

## Why The Spatial Term Matters

The spatial regularization does not smooth the spectra directly. It acts on the
component weights in \(A\):

$$
\sum_{i,j} w_{ij}(A_{ic}-A_{jc})^2
$$

for each selected component \(c\). In practice this:

- suppresses salt-and-pepper weight maps
- stabilizes the decomposition under noise
- encourages extended components to remain spatially coherent
- leaves distant spaxels free to differ because the kernel weight decays with distance

## Compact-Source Components

Selected components can also receive a sparsity prior

$$
\|A_{:,c}\|_1
$$

which is useful when a component is expected to be compact rather than smooth.
This is the mechanism currently used to test GC-like components against a
smooth galaxy/background decomposition.

## Optimization

The torch implementation follows a simple projected-gradient strategy:

1. Initialize \(A\) and \(S\) randomly with positive entries.
2. Optimize the loss with Adam.
3. Clamp \(A\) and \(S\) to remain non-negative after each step.
4. Return spectra, component weights, and the reconstruction \(AS\).

## Sanity Checks

The current tests enforce two baseline conditions:

- setting `lambda_spatial = 0` recovers the original smooth NMF objective
- adding sparse priors improves recovery of compact-source components on a synthetic IFU mock

See [Getting Started](getting-started.qmd) for code examples and
[Benchmark](benchmark.qmd) for the current real-cube test.
